41 European countries, one shade each: tonnes of CO₂ per person in 2023. The range runs from 1.6 in Albania to 13.0 in Faeroe Is. — a factor of 8.3. The median is 5.1.

East first. The darkest block on the map is central Europe — and it is not one thing: Czechia at 7.7 sits next to Hungary at 4.2, 3.5 tonnes apart across one border.

Now west, to something the first frame could not show you. Luxembourg emits 10.3 tonnes a person — the second-highest figure here — and is painted on a shape 1.3% of this map's width.

Back out. 13 of the 41 sit within 1 tonne of the median: 30.8% of the painted land, spanning 1.5 tonnes of a 11.5-tonne range. Most of this map is one colour doing very little work.
